what: Number to Words turns a number written in digits, such as 1,234.56, into English words, such as "One thousand two hundred thirty-four point five six". It also has a check mode that writes an amount the way it goes on a bank check: "One thousand two hundred thirty-four dollars and 56/100".

It helps when you write checks, invoices, contracts, receipts or legal documents where amounts must also appear in words, when teachers and students practise reading large numbers, and when you just want to know how to say a very long number. It handles whole numbers up to 18 digits, decimals and negative numbers.
The words are created in your browser as you type; nothing is sent to a server.
uses: Get the exact wording for the amount line of a check, with cents written as a fraction.
Many formal documents state amounts in figures and in words to prevent mistakes or fraud.
See how large numbers are grouped into thousand, million and billion, and where hyphens go.
Style guides often say to write numbers in words at the start of a sentence.
Find out how to say a number like 7,500,000,000 (seven billion five hundred million).
tutorial: Click the "Number" box and type digits, for example 1234.56. You can include commas, spaces or a $ sign; they are ignored. A minus sign at the start makes the number negative.
The words appear in the box below at once and change with every key you press. The first letter is a capital so you can paste it at the start of a line.
Use "Write as". "Number" writes the whole number in words and reads each decimal digit one by one after "point", for example 3.14 becomes "Three point one four".

Choose "Dollars and cents (for checks)". The whole part becomes dollars in words and the cents are written as a fraction out of 100, for example 250.5 becomes "Two hundred fifty dollars and 50/100". The amount is rounded to whole cents, so use no more than two decimal places.
The whole-number part can have up to 18 digits, which reaches into the quadrillions (up to 999,999,999,999,999,999). Longer numbers show an error.
Click "Copy" to copy the words, then paste them into your check-writing app, invoice or document.
features: Words update as you type, with no button to press.
Writes dollars in words and cents as a fraction, the standard US check format.
Reads decimal digits one by one after the word "point".
Adds "minus" in front of numbers below zero.
Handles thousand, million, billion, trillion and quadrillion.
Commas, spaces and dollar signs are removed automatically.

example.title: Worked example: writing a rent check
example.text: Your rent is $1,850.75. Type 1,850.75 in the Number box. With "Write as" set to "Number" you see "One thousand eight hundred fifty point seven five". Switch to "Dollars and cents (for checks)" and it becomes "One thousand eight hundred fifty dollars and 75/100". Write that on the long line of the check and draw a line through the empty space after it so nothing can be added.

tips: In check mode, an amount of exactly 1 gives "One dollar"; every other amount uses "dollars".
Type a whole amount like 500 in check mode to get "Five hundred dollars and 00/100".
Hyphens are used for numbers from twenty-one to ninety-nine, as in standard American English.
Leading zeros are ignored, so 007 is read as seven.
If you need to write a currency other than dollars, use "Number" mode and add the currency name yourself.
problems: "Enter a number using digits, for example 1234.56."
The box contains letters or symbols other than commas, spaces and $. Type only digits, one decimal point and an optional minus sign.
"That number is too large. The limit is 18 digits."
The whole-number part is longer than 18 digits. Shorten it or split it into parts.
"Use at most two decimal places for dollars and cents."
A value like 9.999 rounds up to a full dollar of cents. Type the amount with at most two decimals, such as 10.00.
Check mode rounds to whole cents, so 4.567 becomes 57/100. Enter the exact amount with two decimals.
